'''''Buy'ce gal, buy'ce tal''''' was a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Alcohol/Legends|drinking]] [[Music/Legends|song]]. By the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], ''Buy'ce gal, buy'ce tal'' had gained significant popularity among numerous Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]].<ref name="TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> The song was cynical in nature, and was an expression of the common Mandalorian [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary's]] wry pragmatism as they accepted that life could be fleeting and victories irrelevant.<ref name="TMPaC" />

Traditionally sung in the Mandalorian [[Language/Legends|dialect]] of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']], ''Buy'ce gal, buy'ce tal'' was a song that contained strong language. When it was performed in the more widely spoken language of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], ''Buy'ce gal, buy'ce tal'' was often given an approximate translation rather than a direct one, with the lyrics edited to be less explicit.<ref name="TZ" />

==Behind the scenes==
First appearing in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[canon]] in the opening of the twenty-first chapter of ''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]'' by [[Karen Traviss]], the song was identified only as a nameless popular Mandalorian drinking chant.<ref name="TZ" /> With the release of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article, ''[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]'', in the magazine's [[Star Wars Insider 86|eighty-sixth issue]], the song was officially deemed "''Buy'ce gal, buy'ce tal''" and a brief interpretation of its lyrical meaning was provided.<ref name="TMPaC" /> In the novel ''Triple Zero'', the translation that is given in Basic is labeled as an "approximate" one, edited for strong language.<ref name="TZ" />
